survivors.claim: HEAD commit 448c93f changed the bespoke difference check to `m[2].trim().length <= 1`, so a non-empty one-character difference is refused as 'names no difference', contradicting D4's 'difference is non-empty'
survivors.impact: A correctly marked bespoke region with a short difference is refused at journey approval, and the threshold landed as an unexplained one-line commit at the head of the range with no test or Decision naming it.
survivors.evidence: Executed: check --matrix over <section data-bespoke="sheet: x"> -> '…onechar.html: data-bespoke="sheet: x" names no difference — say what prevents reuse' exit=1; the same with 'sheet: xy' -> no bespoke finding. Spec D4 line 38: '<difference> is non-empty'. git show 448c93f: '-      } else if (!m || !m[2].trim()) {' / '+      } else if (!m || m[2].trim().length <= 1) {'

survivors.impact: The per-screen kit count is wrong and an unmarked region can pass journey approval unexamined on any mock without a shell whose first region is a kit instance.
